title: fix(gateway): sessions stay busy for subscribers after a Gateway-started run ends
body:
Fixes #177065

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `sessions.subscribe` clients keep showing a session as busy after a Gateway-started backend run, such as an exec completion notice, finishes.

## User Impact

Subscribers receive the settled activity update without waiting for another message. The existing Gateway projection computes current aggregate activity, so overlapping work can still keep the session busy. No configuration, migration, or client protocol changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The terminal backend event can precede release of the session controller's execution ownership. RPC-started runs publish a settled update from their finalizers, but autonomous runs have no such finalizer. The existing controller release now emits `agent.input.settled` through the runtime lifecycle event pipeline after releasing custody. Backend-free maintenance and operations claimed by an RPC source stay quiet.

The maintainer update merges main through `4ee4606426786` without rebasing, keeps the contributor's production fix, and resolves the lifecycle-test conflict using main's slimmed fixtures. One regression table exercises autonomous backend completion, backend-free maintenance, and RPC backend completion through the real turn owner. The RPC lookup runs once at owner settlement, not on streaming events; exact operation matching also covers sources retained across owner rekeying.

Thanks @ayaangazali for the original fix and regression. The contributor commit remains in this PR's history.

## Evidence

- Source and history confirm the gap on main at `4ee4606426786`: the common release path has no settled event; RPC finalizers publish one separately.
- Regression: `publishes settlement only for autonomous backend turns (%s)` in `src/sessions/session-controller.lifecycle.test.ts`, with `maintenance`, `autonomous`, and `rpc` cases. The autonomous case requires an event absent on main; the other cases guard unwanted extra publication.
- Changed-file oxlint and oxfmt pass; `git diff --check` against main passes.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean; no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings on the resolved change. The final main merge leaves the reviewed production and regression diff unchanged. Code and tests were not executed during review.
- Exact-head [PR CI run 39591892416](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39591892416) passed at `84b698c868be9c8e5663e015916fa1756f5f0eef`: all 54 executed jobs passed, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, with no failures or retries. CI covers the regression, affected session/Gateway suites, types, and repository checks; no local test pass is claimed.
- Live Gateway/model proof and local tests/typechecks were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. The previous ClawSweeper hold asked only for live proof and had no code findings; PR CI is the proof for this maintainer update.

Production +16/-0; tests +49/-0; docs +0/-0 against main. The small production increase adds the missing lifecycle notification; unrelated deletions were not used to offset it.
